analysis.title: Pentair Plc (PNR): Pool stabilization a positive first step; Taco exceeding early expectations; Neutral
key_insights: PNR reported 3Q26 revenue of $976mn and non-GAAP EPS of $1.18, above GS estimates and Factset consensus of $964mn/$1.07. Adjusted EPS also exceeded company guidance.

Management says the Pool channel destocking that began in 2Q is complete. About $280mn of Pool inventory left the channel in 2Q ($190mn) and 3Q ($90mn). Year-end channel inventories are expected to be about $180mn below the prior year.

For 2027, management expects Pool sell-through of $1.45bn, implying about 14% yoy growth and in line with its pre-destock 2026 expectation. This assumes no end-market recovery and no share recapture benefit.
Pool ROS is expected to be about 30% in 2027, versus about 34% in 2025. GS reads the outlook as including about 2% realized pricing and a conservative volume decline of low single digits.

PNR has communicated about 3%-4% price increases to dealers for 2027. It is also raising spending on regional sales coverage, dealer support, quality and product innovation, aiming to recapture product placements on its installed base of pool pads. Management says this is not a pricing-led share recapture strategy.

Taco, which closed 10/1, is tracking ahead of expectations. Management now expects about $560mn of 2026 revenue (up about 23% yoy) and more than $620mn in 2027 (10%+ growth). EBITDA is expected to rise from about $90mn in 2026 to more than $105mn in 2027.
Taco growth is led by its commercial and industrial businesses, with residential growing mid-single digits. Management sees cross-selling opportunities through Taco's rep channel.

FY2026 revenue guidance now calls for a decline of about 3% yoy (vs. down 4%-7% prior), including Taco. Adjusted EPS midpoint of about $4.70 is reaffirmed. 4Q26 guidance is sales growth of about 7%-9% and adjusted EPS of about $1.15, versus GS/consensus of $1.26/$1.21.

Segment results: Flow sales rose 4% yoy to $262mn with ROS up 250bps to 26.2%. Water Solutions sales rose 1% to $422mn with ROS up 370bps to 28.7%. Pool sales fell 18% to $291mn, better than management expected, with segment income down 38% and margin at 24.6%.
3Q26 included $8mn of tariff refunds, versus $35mn in 2Q26. Adjusted ROS for PNR fell 90bps to 24.8% on inflation, partly offset by productivity, and beat the GS 23.1% view.
PNR enters 4Q26 at about 2.5x pro forma net leverage after the Taco deal and expects to delever toward its typical 1.5x-2.0x range over the next 24 months.

GS raised its 12-month price target to $66 from $60, based on an unchanged 12x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS. The increase reflects updated estimates and the Taco acquisition. The rating stays Neutral, with 6.0% upside from $62.29.
GS adjusted EPS estimates for 2026E/2027E/2028E move 0%/8%/9% to $4.70/$5.17/$5.53, mostly from adding Taco to the model. 2027E revenue rises 16% to $4,803mn.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised its target to $66 from $60 on higher estimates and the Taco acquisition, keeping 12x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS. Pool destocking is complete and Taco is ahead of plan, but end-market conditions remain mixed.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported: revenue $976.4mn vs GS est $963.6mn. Non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.18 vs GS/Factset consensus est $1.07. GAAP basic EPS $0.91 vs est $1.00. EBITDA $257.3mn vs est $242.2mn.
4Q26 guidance: adjusted EPS about $1.15 vs GS est $1.26 and consensus est $1.21. Sales growth about 7%-9% yoy including Taco, implying revenue of about $1.10bn vs GS/consensus est about $1.0bn.

FY2026 guidance: revenue down about 3% yoy (about $4.05bn) vs GS est $3.9bn and consensus est $4.0bn. Adjusted EPS midpoint about $4.70 reaffirmed. Pool outlook is down 18%-19% (vs down 18%-22% prior), Flow up MSD, Water Solutions up HSD.
3Q26 SG&A was $175.9mn vs GS est $136.7mn, and net income (GAAP) was $145.1mn vs est $160.6mn. Free cash flow was $152.3mn vs est $160.5mn.
risk_factors: Underlying pool end-market conditions remain mixed, and the 2027 Pool framework does not assume a market recovery
Higher leverage of about 2.5x pro forma net debt after the Taco acquisition

tension_points.bull_case: Destocking is complete and management guides 2027 Pool sell-through of $1.45bn (about 14% growth) with about 30% ROS. This assumes no end-market recovery and no share recapture, so GS sees a straightforward earnings recovery.
tension_points.bear_case: Underlying end-market conditions remain mixed. Pool ROS of about 30% is below the roughly 34% of 2025, and the guide implies pricing of about 2% with volume down low single digits.

theme_stances.key_argument: With the Pool destock complete, PNR gave greater visibility into a 2027 Pool recovery that does not depend on an improvement in underlying pool demand.
theme_stances.evidence: Pool destock complete, shifting the debate from channel inventory to share recovery
